paper.title: Information-Theoretic Confidence Bounds for Reinforcement Learning

unmapped: Gaussian prior N(mu_1, Sigma_1) on theta
reward is r(Y) for a known bounded (range B), nondecreasing, 1-Lipschitz function r of the observation
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{A} \subset \Re^d$ be a finite action set, and assume that $\sup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \|a\|_2 \leq 1$. We assume a $N(\mu_1, \Sigma_1)$ prior over the model parameter $\theta \in \Re^d$. At time $\ell$, an action $A_\ell \in \mathcal{A}$ is selected, and $Y_{\ell, A_\ell} = \theta^\top A_\ell + w_\ell$ is observed, where $w_\ell $ are i.i.d. $N(0, \sigma_w^2)$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning in finite-horizon MDPs, not a bandit problem.
unmapped: episodic finite-horizon MDP with horizon tau, L episodes
Bernoulli rewards with Beta priors, Dirichlet transition priors (Assumption 2 on prior parameters)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of learning to optimize a random finite-horizon MDP $M = (\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, R, P, \tau, \rho)$ in repeated episodes.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning in factored MDPs, not a bandit problem.
unmapped: factored MDP with known scopes, m reward factors, n transition factors, factor domain sizes at most K
settings.definition_quote: A factored MDP is an MDP with factored rewards and transitions.

bound.expression_latex: \Gamma \sqrt{ L ~I(\theta; A_1, Y_{1, A_1}, \dots, A_{L}, Y_{L, A_{L}}) } +B, \Gamma = 4 \sqrt{ \frac{\sigma_{1, \max}^2}{\log(1 + \frac{\sigma_{1, \max}^2}{\sigma_w^2})} \log(4 |\mathcal{A}| L) }

symbols.sigma_1max: sqrt(max_a a^T Sigma_1 a), prior predictive std of the mean reward
symbols.sigma_w: standard deviation of the Gaussian noise
symbols.I_T: mutual information I(theta; A_1, Y_1, ..., A_L, Y_L) between parameter and history
symbols.B_rew: range bound of the reward function (Assumption 1)

conditions: reward function r bounded with range B, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz

source.label: prop:linear-bandit-regret
source.quote: Under the assumptions stated in Section \ref{sec:linear-bandits}, the Bayesian regret of Thompson sampling and UCB over $L$ periods is \[ \mathbb{E}[{\rm Regret}(L, \pi)] \leq \Gamma \sqrt{ L ~I(\theta; A_1, Y_{1, A_1}, \dots, A_{L}, Y_{L, A_{L}}) } +B \] where \[ \Gamma = 4 \sqrt{ \frac{\sigma_{1, \max}^2}{\log\left(1 + \frac{\sigma_{1, \max}^2}{\sigma_w^2}\right)} \log(4 |\mathcal{A}| L) }. \]

results.notes: L = T, |A| = K. Lemma (lemma:linear-bandit-information) bounds I_T <= (d/2) log(1 + lambda_max T / sigma_w^2), giving O(sqrt(d T log K) log T) per the text. TS does not need delta; it's an analysis choice.

source.label: prop:mdp-regret
source.quote: The Bayesian regret of Thompson sampling and UCB over $L$ episodes is \[ \mathbb{E}[{\rm Regret}(L, \pi)] = \tilde{O} \left( \tau \sqrt{\tau L ~I(M; \mu_1, Y_{1, \mu_1}, \dots, \mu_{L}, Y_{L, \mu_{L}}) } \right). \]

results.notes: Out-of-scope RL. Lemma 10 bounds I_M <= (|S|+2)|S||A| log(1+T/(|S||A|)).

symbols.I_M: mutual information between MDP M and the history
